chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, who said:

I asked Abu Al-Hasan Al-Reza (peace be upon him) about the faith and the Islam. So he (peace be upon him) said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Rather it is the Islam, and the faith is above it by a level, and the piety is above the faith by a level, and the conviction is above the piety by a level; and there has not been distributed among the people anything scarcer than the conviction.' He said, I said, 'So which thing is the conviction?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The reliance upon Allah, and the submission to Allah, and the pleasure with the decree of Allah, and the delegation to Allah.' I said, 'So what is the interpretation of that?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'That is how Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual hierarchy of Islam, faith, piety, and conviction in Shia theology?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the chain of al-Kulayni, establishes a distinct spiritual hierarchy where Yaqin (certainty) stands above Taqwa (piety), reflecting the Shia emphasis on inner conviction as the culmination of faith. It defines this supreme state as Tawakkul (reliance) and Ridha (contentment) with divine decree, a concept deeply rooted in the teachings of Imam al-Sadiq. The rarity of this level is highlighted to underscore the depth of spiritual maturity required for true submission to God's will.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus who said,

‘I asked Abu Al-Hassan Al-Rezaasws about the Emān and the Islām. So heasws said: ‘Abu Ja’farasws said: ‘But rather it is the Islām, and the Emān is above it by a level, and ‘التَّقْوَى’ the piety is above the Emān by a level, and ‘الْيَقِينَ’ the conviction if above the piety by a level; and there has not been distributed between the people anything scarcer than ‘الْيَقِينَ’ the conviction’. He (the narrator) said, ‘So which thing is ‘الْيَقِينَ’ the conviction?’ Heasws said: ‘The reliance upon Allahazwj, and the submission to Allahazwj, and the pleasure with whatever Allahazwj has Judged, and the delegation (of the matters) to Allahazwj’. I said, ‘So what is the interpretation of that?’ Heasws said: ‘That is how Abu Ja’farasws said it’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Yunus who has said the following:

“I asked abu al-Hassan al-Rida (a.s.) about belief and Islam and he said, abu Ja’far (a.s.) has said the following: ‘There is Islam. Belief is one degree higher above Islam, and piety is one degree higher above belief. Certainty is by one degree higher above piety and nothing is distributed among people so little as certainty is.’ I then said, ‘What then is certainty?’ The Imam said, ‘It is trust in Allah, submission to Allah, accepting the decision of Allah and allowing Allah to be the person in charge of one’s affairs.’ I then said, ‘What then is the interpretation of that?’ The Imam said, ‘This is how abu Ja’far (a.s.) said it is.’”
